name: Bookends & Beginnings
dek: An independent bookstore that still behaves like a civic institution.
summary: A Main Street bookstore whose events calendar doubles as a public square. The shop is one of the businesses watching Church Street Plaza and the Main Street Lofts conversion.

name: Evanston Farmers Market
dek: Saturday mornings, University Plaza, weather permitting and often not.
summary: The year-round market is downtown’s most reliable crowd. Any Fountain Square plan that ignores Saturday will learn otherwise by June.

name: Union Pizzeria
dek: A neighborhood dining room on the independent mile.
summary: A Main Street dining room that treats the block as its dining room. The proposed lofts upstairs would share an alley the kitchen already uses at 10 p.m.

name: Larsen’s Bakery
dek: Cardamom, rye, and a Central Street morning that has not changed its mind.
summary: A family bakery on Central Street and a reminder that Evanston’s commercial life is not only downtown. Demo portrait of a North Shore morning business.

name: The Celery Stalk
dek: A lunch counter that still knows the names of the people who plan the city.
summary: A Sherman Avenue lunch counter across from the civic buildings. Plan Commission packets have been marked up at these tables for twenty years.

name: Downtown Evanston Partnership
dek: The civic business league that speaks for the square.
summary: A business improvement organization that programs the plaza, advocates for retail, and will have a great deal to say about whatever Fountain Square becomes.
